To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
outflows preferentially expel material with low angular momentum and that this can lead to pure disc systems.

(i) galactic outflows can significantly reduce the angular momentum of gas in dwarf galaxies, and (ii) the combination of this effect with a high redshift star formation peak and a reservoir of high angular material can lead to the formation of pure disc galaxies with no bulge.

high redshift gas flows have low angular momentum and are expelled perpendicular to the disc plane, and that these outflows remove low angular momentum gas, preventing the formation of a classical bulge.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the formation and evolution of low mass galaxies in a cosmological context.
the role of outflows in the hierarchical formation of dwarf galaxies.
the hierarchical formation of galaxies and their dark matter haloes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the formation of bulge-less disc galaxies is a natural consequence of the hierarchical growth of dark matter halos and the associated star formation and outflows.
the hierarchical formation of bulge-less galaxies in a Lambda CDM Universe is possible, but it requires the presence of outflows.

hierarchical galaxy formation is a complex, non-linear process which is highly sensitive to the initial conditions of a galaxy and its environment, with a large number of possible evolutionary paths to the final, observed, galaxy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the angular momentum distribution of baryons in low-mass galaxies is strongly modified by outflows, which preferentially remove material of low angular momentum and thus allow the formation of disc-dominated systems.
outflows are the primary mechanism responsible for removing low angular momentum gas and thus allowing the formation of bulge-less galaxies in low-mass haloes.
outflows are the key mechanism that allows pure disc galaxies to exist in a Lambda cold DM universe.
The main takeaway from our work is that
outflows can play an important role in the formation of bulge-less galaxies by removing gas with low angular momentum.

outflows are not only important for the chemical enrichment of galaxies, but also have a major effect on the angular momentum distribution of the baryons and thus the formation of bulge-less galaxies.

outflows are a key ingredient in the formation of low angular momentum discs, a result with implications for the formation of low surface brightness galaxies, the evolution of the stellar mass function with redshift and the nature of the faintest galaxies detected in the early Universe.
